properties.from_note: Before 'Abd al-Rahman's reign the Fur sultans had no fixed capital, so for earlier relations (rel-fur-01 Sulayman Solongdungu, rel-fur-04 Ya'qub / 'Umar Lel) al-Fashir is an anachronistic symbol of the sultanate.
properties.to_note: Uri is the better-attested centre in the text but has no Wikidata item found; Ain Farah is the Wikidata-listed site the same page ties to the Tunjur. Both rest on Arkell's hypotheses as reported by Kropacek.
properties.label_en: Sulayman Solongdungu, probably the dynasty's founder, drove out the Tunjur and annexed the area around Jebel Marra.
properties.label_ar: طرد سليمان سولونج، المرجح أنه مؤسس الأسرة، التنجر وضم المنطقة حول جبل مرة. [Arabic text pending native-speaker review.]

properties.from_note: Before 'Abd al-Rahman's reign the Fur sultans had no fixed capital, so for earlier relations (rel-fur-01 Sulayman Solongdungu, rel-fur-04 Ya'qub / 'Umar Lel) al-Fashir is an anachronistic symbol of the sultanate.
properties.to_note: The registered source names Wara as capital of the Tunjur-era Wadai kingdom, not explicitly of the 17th–18th-century sultanate in rel-fur-04. Wikidata Q1132786 (Ouaddai Empire) lists a capital (P36) but I did not use an unsourced claim.
properties.label_en: Sultan Ya'qub of Wadai invaded as far as Kabkabiyya and was driven out; in the mid-18th century Wadai defeated 'Umar Lel's army and captured the sultan.
properties.label_ar: غزا سلطان وداي يعقوب حتى كبكابية وطُرد، وفي منتصف القرن الثامن عشر هزمت وداي جيش عمر ليل وأسرت السلطان. [Arabic text pending native-speaker review.]
